title: The rank of a lisse sheaf is locally constant
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its $\ell$-adic topology [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and put $E_X=p_X^*\underline E$ [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Let $L$ be an $E_X$-module sheaf [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] that is lisse: it is locally isomorphic to $E_U^{\oplus n}$, for finite $n\geq0$, on a covering of the small pro-etale site [sk-def-pe-site]. For $r\geq0$, let $X_r\subseteq|X|$ consist of points $x$ such that, for some (equivalently every) object $U\to X$ in a trivializing covering with $x$ in its image, $L|_U$ has rank $r$ near a preimage of $x$. This rank is independent of the trivializing covering and of the preimage. Then the $X_r$ are open and closed, only finitely many are nonempty if $X$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], and $X=\coprod_{r\geq0}X_r$, with $L|_{X_r}$ of constant rank $r$. Each $X_r$ is given its open subscheme structure [def-weil-open-immersion].

proof.text: Choose a pro-etale trivializing cover $\{U_i\to X\}$ with $L|_{U_i}\simeq E_{U_i}^{\oplus n_i}$, using [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]. It is an fpqc cover by [sk-def-pe-site]. On $W=U_i\times_XU_j$, [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients](1) identifies the two restrictions with $E_W^{\oplus n_i}$ and $E_W^{\oplus n_j}$. Apply [lem-sfb-continuous-coefficient-free-rank]: if $W$ is nonempty, $n_i=n_j$. Thus unequal labels have empty overlaps. This includes rank zero and requires no finite index set.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 2: locally constant rank and fpqc descent of open subsets; assembled from the two extracted arguments

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-fpqc-labelled-clopen-descent] with $A=\mathbf N$ and $\rho_i\equiv n_i$ to obtain a clopen partition $(O_r)$, with preimage in $U_i$ whole if $n_i=r$ and empty otherwise. For any further trivializing object $V\to X$ of rank $s$, the same overlap comparison of step 1 gives $n_i=s$ on every nonempty $U_i\times_XV$. The test-morphism clause of that descent lemma, with $\sigma\equiv s$, gives preimage of $O_r$ in $V$ whole if $s=r$ and empty otherwise. Apply this to every constant-rank neighborhood in any trivializing covering. The unique piece containing a point is therefore its rank at every preimage in every trivialization. Hence $X_r=O_r$ with exactly the characterization in the statement.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 2: locally constant rank and fpqc descent of open subsets; assembled from the two extracted arguments

proof.text: Give $X_r$ its open subscheme structure. By [lem-galois-fpqc-covering-base-change] the restrictions $U_i\times_XX_r\to X_r$ form an fpqc cover, and [sk-lem-pe-weakly-etale-stability] and [sk-def-pe-site] make it a pro-etale cover. A nonempty member has $n_i=r$ by step 2. Pulling back its trivialization via [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients](1) gives the rank-$r$ free module; an empty member has the unique zero module and the same assertion. Thus $L|_{X_r}$ has constant rank $r$. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] the coproduct of these schemes exists. Its canonical map to $X$ is an isomorphism: on the disjoint open pieces it is the identity, so these inverse identities agree on empty intersections and glue.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 2: locally constant rank and fpqc descent of open subsets; assembled from the two extracted arguments

proof.text: If $X$ is quasi-compact, its open cover $\{X_r\}$ has a finite subcover by [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Disjointness forces every piece outside that finite subcover to be empty. If $X$ is empty, all pieces are empty. No finiteness of the original trivializing cover was used.
